A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Talk2DINO paper and complete Appendices A–D. All 20 pages were compared through text extraction and rendering; the only visible difference is the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v2 reports original segmentation benchmarks and ablations in Tables 1–4, plus supplementary experiments, image-text retrieval results and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including segmentation evaluations in Section 4 and retrieval experiments in Appendix B, Table 8.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same CLIP-to-DINOv2 projection, attention-head selection, InfoNCE training objective, segmentation inference and background-cleaning procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same COCO Captions training data, eight segmentation benchmark configurations, COCO retrieval evaluation and in-the-wild qualitative examples.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding comparisons, including Tables 1, 7, 8 and 10. FreeDA, ProxyCLIP, CLIP-DINOiser and dino.txt are already present in v2.

E3.justification: Training budgets, backbone configurations, evaluation splits, metrics, resizing and sliding-window protocols, refinement settings and supplementary experimental procedures are identical.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and the appendices retain identical backbone, projection, attention-selection, background-cleaning, text-token and resolution analyses, alongside the same activation visualizations and qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. Statistical and uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match. For example, Table 1 retains average mIoU values of 46.3 and 46.1 for the base and large models with mask refinement; supplementary results also remain identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical task formulation and method equations in Section 3 are identical, including the projection, attention aggregation, contrastive objective and background shaping.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about bridging CLIP and DINOv2 without backbone fine-tuning, improving localization and achieving state-of-the-art unsupervised segmentation.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning attention artifacts, backbone and text-token limitations, model scaling, resolution robustness and retrieval behavior are unchanged in the main text and appendices.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, processing instructions and the code/model access link are identical. The arXiv hyperlink changes only to identify the later paper version.

R1.justification: Section 2, supplementary comparisons with prior work and all 65 reference entries are identical. No citations or research-positioning statements were added or removed.

P1.justification: The first-page marginal stamp changes from v2, dated 5 Aug 2025, to v3, dated 16 Sep 2025. This is a minor document-label edit; the prose, headings and section structure are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–12, Tables 1–10, captions and page layout are unchanged. Rendered pages match exactly outside the first-page version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the entire scientific content, evidence, explanations and presentation of v2, including its appendices. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
